name: x402 CLI Cast Access Without Node
query: Access this Radius testnet x402-gated endpoint once from the terminal. I have a funded Foundry keystore account named radius-payer and wallet address 0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111. Do not create a Node project or JavaScript script.
context: The user wants a one-off paid request to an existing x402 endpoint. They explicitly want a terminal flow and already have a funded Foundry keystore account. The endpoint returns x402 v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED headers and supports Radius testnet with EIP-2612 gas sponsoring.
expected_behavior: Uses the x402 CLI/cast reference rather than the viem app-client flow
Uses curl, jq, base64, python3, and cast; does not create a package.json, Node project, or JavaScript script
Fetches the endpoint once without payment and reads the PAYMENT-REQUIRED response header
Base64-decodes PAYMENT-REQUIRED and selects accepts[0] as the singular accepted object
Reads the EIP-2612 nonce with cast call against SBC nonces(address)(uint256)
Generates a random Permit2 nonce with a shell-friendly snippet
Builds EIP-2612 and Permit2 typed-data JSON without relying on repo-relative template paths
Includes EIP712Domain in typed-data types for cast signing
Signs both typed-data files with cast wallet sign --data --from-file --account radius-payer
Builds the final PAYMENT-SIGNATURE payload with accepted, payload.permit2Authorization, and extensions.eip2612GasSponsoring.info
Keeps final payload uint256-like fields as decimal strings
Sends PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and decodes PAYMENT-RESPONSE for inspection
success_criteria: No raw private key is requested, logged, or passed as a CLI argument
The server response field accepts is not sent directly as a top-level accepts field in the client payload
The client payload uses singular accepted
EIP-2612 spender is the Permit2 contract 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3
Permit2 spender is the x402 Proxy 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001
Network uses eip155:72344 and chain ID 72344 for Radius testnet
The flow can be run from an arbitrary project directory
